packages.label: תּוֹרָה וְאָדָם
packages.reason: Torah and Adam (the human being) share the same essential nature: reaching the true Torah IS reaching the true human form. They are not cause-and-effect — one does not produce the other. Rather, they are two expressions of the same divine reality. The verse 'זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה אָדָם' (Num. 19:14) declares their identity. Just as there are multiple levels of representing a human being (written word, drawing, wooden sculpture, the actual person), so there are levels of Torah knowledge — and only the innermost, true Torah is the true Adam. The Torah's entire argument is built on this bechina identity.
